name: Lithium
description: A soft, highly reactive Group 1 metal used in batteries and specialty alloys.

name: Sodium
description: A very reactive Group 1 metal whose vapor gives a yellow flame and whose compounds are ubiquitous.

name: Potassium
description: An extremely reactive Group 1 metal essential to biology in ionic form.

name: Rubidium
description: A soft, silvery alkali metal used in research and atomic clocks.

name: Cesium
description: A low-melting alkali metal famous for its extreme reactivity and precise clock standards.

name: Francium
description: A highly radioactive alkali metal known only in trace amounts.

name: Fluorine
description: The most electronegative element, appearing as a pale yellow diatomic gas.

name: Chlorine
description: A greenish-yellow diatomic gas widely used in disinfectants and industrial chemistry.

name: Bromine
description: A reddish-brown liquid halogen notable as one of the few liquid elements at room temperature.

name: Iodine
description: A dark solid halogen that sublimes readily to a violet vapor.

name: Astatine
description: A rare, highly radioactive halogen with very limited direct observation.

name: Tennessine
description: A synthetic superheavy halogen whose properties are inferred from brief production.

name: Iron
description: A common transition metal that forms many vividly colored coordination compounds.

name: Copper
description: A reddish transition metal prized for electrical conductivity and colored salts.

name: Nickel
description: A corrosion-resistant transition metal used in stainless steels and catalysts.

name: Cobalt
description: A transition metal whose ions and compounds often show deep blue colors.

name: Chromium
description: A hard transition metal associated with brilliant oxidation-state color chemistry.

name: Manganese
description: A transition metal with many oxidation states and important metallurgical uses.

name: Aluminum
description: A light, abundant metal whose oxide is amphoteric and protective.

name: Gallium
description: A soft post-transition metal that can melt in the hand.

name: Indium
description: A malleable post-transition metal used in semiconductors and coatings.

name: Tin
description: A post-transition metal famous for bronze and for forming multiple allotropes.

name: Lead
description: A dense post-transition metal known for toxicity, dense shielding, and colorful pigments in compounds.

name: Bismuth
description: A brittle post-transition metal whose oxide and salts can show striking iridescent colors.

name: Ozone
description: A triatomic allotrope of oxygen that behaves as a strongly oxidizing atmospheric gas.

name: Hydrogen
description: A colorless diatomic gas and the lightest element.

name: Nitrogen
description: A very stable diatomic gas that dominates Earth’s atmosphere.

name: Oxygen
description: A diatomic gas essential for combustion and aerobic life.

name: Selenium
description: An element with multiple structural forms and important semiconductor chemistry.

name: Tellurium
description: A metalloid-like element often discussed alongside sulfur and selenium chemistry.

name: Copper(II) sulfate
description: A bright blue salt used in laboratories and agriculture.

name: Potassium permanganate
description: A deep purple oxidizing salt of manganese.

name: Chromium(III) oxide
description: A green chromium compound widely recognized for its pigment-like color.

name: Nickel(II) sulfate
description: A greenish nickel salt used in plating baths and electrochemistry.

name: Cobalt(II) chloride
description: A blue-to-pink indicator salt often used in moisture-sensitive contexts.

name: Lead(II) iodide
description: A bright yellow precipitate formed from lead and iodide ions.

name: Carbon dioxide
description: A nonmetal oxide that dissolves in water to give carbonic acid.

name: Sulfur dioxide
description: A pungent acidic oxide responsible for part of acid rain chemistry.

name: Sulfur trioxide
description: A highly reactive acidic oxide that is a key precursor to sulfuric acid.

name: Nitrogen dioxide
description: A brown acidic oxide and air pollutant formed in high-temperature combustion.

name: Phosphorus pentoxide
description: A powerful desiccant and acidic oxide of phosphorus.

name: Silicon dioxide
description: A network solid oxide that forms quartz and many silicate minerals.

name: Graphite
description: A layered allotrope of carbon used in pencils and electrodes.

name: Diamond
description: A hard tetrahedral allotrope of carbon with exceptional thermal conductivity.

name: White phosphorus
description: A highly reactive phosphorus allotrope that oxidizes readily in air.

name: Red phosphorus
description: A more stable phosphorus allotrope used in safety matches.

name: Rhombic sulfur
description: A crystalline allotrope of sulfur stable at room temperature.

name: Monoclinic sulfur
description: A higher-temperature crystalline allotrope of sulfur.
